recent_posts.title: Animated icons for React, without the setup pain
recent_posts.summary: @animateicons/react is a new npm package providing animated Lucide-style icons for React applications. It aims to simplify adding motion details to buttons, menus, dashboards, and landing pages without building custom SVG animations from scratch. Installation is via pnpm/npm and usage follows a straightforward named import pattern from the package.

recent_posts.title: OpenChoreo: The Open-Source Developer Platform for Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: OpenChoreo is a CNCF sandbox open-source Internal Developer Platform (IDP) built on Kubernetes. It features a modular multi-plane architecture separating control, data, build, and observability concerns. Platform engineers can define secure golden paths via programmable Kubernetes-native abstractions, while developers get a Backstage-powered portal, declarative GitOps, and built-in SRE and FinOps agents. The project is community-driven and invites contributions, feature requests, and early adoption.

recent_posts.title: Noderax — Infrastructure Control Plane
recent_posts.summary: Noderax is an open-source, self-hosted infrastructure control plane for managing Linux servers. It replaces fragmented SSH sessions, shell scripts, and cron jobs with a unified interface. Key features include one-line setup, one-click node bootstrap, real-time telemetry, browser-based terminal access, task scheduling, package operations, and workspace-level RBAC, MFA, and SSO support. A lightweight agent is installed on each server and communicates with the central control plane.

recent_posts.title: Control Spotify and Youtube from the System tray, Quick Media Controls Free and Opensource Native Windows Application
recent_posts.summary: Quick Media Controls is a free, open-source native Windows tray application that lets you control any media playing on your PC (Spotify, YouTube, etc.) without opening the player. It supports customizable keybindings, mouse click actions, light/dark mode, and Windows accent color theming. Available on the Microsoft Store and GitHub.

recent_posts.title: Supabase just hit 100k stars on Github
recent_posts.summary: Supabase has crossed 100,000 GitHub stars, placing it among the top 100 most starred repositories. The author shares their personal experience using Supabase as a default backend choice, highlighting its all-in-one feature set (auth, storage, realtime, edge functions), its foundation on trusted open-source tech like Postgres, excellent local development experience, clean CLI and JS client, polished Studio UI, solid docs, and a generous free tier.

recent_posts.title: [Open Source] I've created a spin-off of FFmpeg-Kit Plugin with ability to deploy custom builds
recent_posts.summary: A Flutter plugin spin-off of FFmpegKit has been released as a fully open source project with support for custom FFmpeg builds. It supports 100+ external FFmpeg libraries, Android, Linux, and Windows platforms, and includes FFmpeg, FFprobe, and FFplay support. The project ships 22 pre-built binaries across Audio, Video, Video+HW, Full, and Base bundles for both GPL and LGPL licenses. A pure C API was added to allow usage from any language via FFI. iOS and macOS support is planned.

recent_posts.title: I made a fork of a fork of Peppermint.sh
recent_posts.summary: A developer forked Pepperminto (itself a fork of Peppermint.sh ticket management) to rescue and modernize a half-built Knowledge Base feature. Over 3.5 days, they consolidated redundant apps, optimized a Turborepo + pnpm monorepo, fixed broken CRUD workflows in the KB engine, refactored the client portal with shadcn/ui and Tailwind, added a slug migration system for SEO-friendly URLs, and overhauled CI/CD with GitHub Actions and multi-arch Docker builds. Known bugs remain, and the roadmap includes full Markdown support, file attachments, dynamic popular topics, and advanced Kanban customization.

recent_posts.title: Turn your VS Code into Black Mesa: A Half-Life Theme & Sounds Extension
recent_posts.summary: A VS Code extension that transforms the editor into a Half-Life themed environment, featuring a custom Lambda color palette, file icons, and a reactive HEV suit audio system. The extension plays game-accurate voice lines in response to coding actions like saving files, triggering terminal errors, or toggling the terminal. A key technical challenge was handling VS Code's asynchronous event system, which caused audio race conditions. The solution involved a custom priority queue and cooldown system in Node.js that delays minor sounds by 50ms and allows high-priority events to cancel lower-priority audio. Available on the VS Code Marketplace and GitHub.

recent_posts.title: Lucide-based Animated Icons (Open Source, shadcn/ui CLI)
recent_posts.summary: AnimateIcons is an open-source collection of 200+ animated SVG icons built on the Lucide design language. The library integrates with shadcn/ui CLI, provides smooth lightweight animations using motion, and focuses on clean UI micro-interactions for React applications. The project is actively seeking community feedback and contributions.

recent_posts.title: Open Source - PodPDF
recent_posts.summary: PodPDF is a lightweight PDF generation library for Node.js and Bun that claims to be 5x faster than jsPDF. It's TypeScript native, has zero dependencies, and comes in at just 8 KB minified, making it an efficient option for server-side PDF creation in JavaScript runtimes.
